voiceDirection: Warm, calm, intimate voice. Slow pace. Honour every [pause Ns] marker as real silence.

sessions.title: Quick reset
script: Welcome. You did the right thing by stopping for a moment.
Wherever you are, set both feet on the floor. Let your back lengthen a little.
[pause 4s]
We'll take three breaths together. Just three. That's enough to help your body ease the pressure.
Breathe in through your nose. Then, without breathing out, sip in a little more air at the top.
Now let it all go, slowly, through your mouth.
[pause 8s]
Once more. In through the nose, and a little extra on top.
Then a long, slow exhale, like a sigh that takes its time.
[pause 9s]
As you breathe out, let your shoulders drop. They don't need to carry anything right now.
[pause 5s]
Last one. A double breath in through the nose.
And release everything, long and slow, through the mouth.
[pause 10s]
Unclench your jaw. Let a little space open between your teeth. Let your tongue rest.
[pause 8s]
Now just breathe at your own pace. Nothing to force.
[pause 12s]
Feel the weight of your body in your seat. Feel your feet on the ground.
You are here. You can get through this moment.
[pause 14s]
One more easy breath, just for you.
[pause 7s]
Whenever you're ready, pick up your day again, one step at a time.

sessions.title: Lower your cortisol
script: Welcome. For the next few minutes, all you need to do is breathe.
Sit or lie down comfortably. If you like, rest one hand on your belly.
[pause 5s]
Close your eyes, or let your gaze settle softly on the floor.
[pause 5s]
Here's something simple to know. When your exhale is longer than your inhale, your body gets a message.
The message is: you're safe, everything is okay. And little by little, your stress response begins to settle.
[pause 4s]
Start by noticing your breath as it is. No need to change it.
[pause 10s]
Now breathe in through your nose for a count of four. One, two, three, four.
And breathe out slowly through your mouth for six. One, two, three, four, five, six.
[pause 5s]
Again. In for four.
[pause 4s]
Out for six, as if you were gently blowing on a candle without putting it out.
[pause 7s]
Keep going at your own pace. Four in, six out.
[pause 25s]
If it feels comfortable, let your exhale stretch a little longer. Seven, or even eight.
No straining. The air just flows out, like a wave pulling back from the shore.
[pause 20s]
With every exhale, let something soften. Your forehead. Your cheeks. Your jaw.
[pause 12s]
Your shoulders sink. Your arms grow heavy. Your hands open.
[pause 12s]
Your belly rises and falls, very gently. Your back lets itself be held.
[pause 20s]
If your mind drifts, that's fine. Just come back to the count. Four in, six out.
[pause 20s]
Notice what has shifted. Maybe a little more slowness. A little more space.
[pause 10s]
Now let your breathing return to its natural rhythm.
[pause 8s]
You can come back to this long, slow breath any time. It's always with you.
Gently move your fingers, and open your eyes whenever you're ready.

sessions.title: Your inner refuge
script: Welcome. Today you're going to create a refuge. A place that's yours alone, to return to whenever life feels too fast.
Get comfortable. Let your back be supported and your hands come to rest.
[pause 5s]
Close your eyes. Take a deep breath in through your nose.
And let it flow out slowly through your mouth.
[pause 7s]
One more time. Breathe in… and let go.
[pause 8s]
Now let a place appear in your mind where you feel completely at peace.
It can be real or imagined. A beach, a forest, a cozy room, a garden. Choose whatever comes.
[pause 15s]
Look around. What colors do you see? What is the light like?
Take your time noticing the details, one by one.
[pause 20s]
Now listen. Maybe there's wind, or water, or birdsong. Or a soft, easy silence.
[pause 20s]
Feel the air on your skin. Is it warm, or cool? Notice what's beneath your feet, or under your hands.
[pause 20s]
Breathe in the scent of this place. Salt, grass, wood, a flower. Let it surround you.
[pause 18s]
There might even be a taste in the air. Or a drink you love, waiting right beside you.
[pause 15s]
Here, nothing is rushing you. No one needs anything from you. You are safe.
Let your body feel that. Your shoulders loosen, your breath slows down.
[pause 30s]
Wander a little through your refuge. Find the exact spot where you feel best, and settle there.
[pause 25s]
Now let's anchor this place. Gently touch your thumb to your index finger, making a small circle.
As your fingers meet, breathe in the calm of your refuge. Its colors, its sounds, its softness.
[pause 20s]
This gesture becomes your key. Later, when you bring these two fingers together, you can find a little of this peace again.
[pause 12s]
You can release your fingers now.
[pause 6s]
Know that this refuge doesn't disappear. It stays inside you, ready to welcome you back.
[pause 10s]
Slowly, come back to the room you're in. Feel the support beneath you.
[pause 6s]
Take a slightly fuller breath. Stretch if you feel like it.
[pause 6s]
And when you're ready, open your eyes, bringing this calm with you.

sessions.title: Panic anchor
script: I'm right here with you. What you're feeling is very uncomfortable, but it isn't dangerous.
It's a wave. It rises, it peaks, and it comes back down. Every time.
[pause 5s]
Set both feet flat on the floor. Press down a little, and feel the ground holding you up.
[pause 6s]
Now press your palms together. Firmly, for a few seconds.
[pause 5s]
And let go. Feel the warmth, the tingling in your hands.
[pause 6s]
Let's breathe together, slowly. In through your nose… two… three… four.
And out… two… three… four… five… six.
[pause 4s]
Again. In… two… three… four.
Out… two… three… four… five… six.
[pause 5s]
Keep this rhythm going. It doesn't have to be perfect.
[pause 15s]
Find something cool or neutral near you. A table, a wall, the back of your phone.
Touch it. Feel its temperature, its texture.
[pause 12s]
If you can, silently name three things you can see. Just their names.
[pause 12s]
Your heart may be racing. That's your body trying to protect you. It will settle.
[pause 6s]
Keep your feet on the floor. Keep your breath long.
[pause 15s]
The wave is already passing. There's nothing more you need to do but breathe.
[pause 15s]
You've made it through this moment. You're here, right now.
[pause 6s]
Take one more long breath out. Then move forward gently, at your own pace.

sessions.title: Desk reset
script: Welcome to this little break. Just three minutes, all for you.
Take your eyes off the screen. Rest them on something far away, or close them.
[pause 5s]
Sit all the way back in your chair. Feet flat, spine tall but relaxed.
[pause 5s]
Take a slow breath in through your nose.
And a long breath out through your mouth.
[pause 7s]
Again. Let the air fill your belly.
Then breathe out, no rush.
[pause 8s]
A third time. Breathe in… and let it all go.
[pause 9s]
Now gently tip your head toward your right shoulder. Feel the left side of your neck stretch.
[pause 8s]
Come back to center, then tip toward the left.
[pause 8s]
Back to center. Lift your shoulders up toward your ears and squeeze a little.
[pause 3s]
And let them drop.
[pause 6s]
Roll your shoulders back slowly, two or three times.
[pause 10s]
Breathe normally. Notice how much lighter your body feels.
[pause 12s]
Before you dive back in, pick just one thing to do next. Only one.
[pause 6s]
Then head back to work with a clearer mind.

sessions.title: After a tense meeting
script: Welcome. That meeting is over, but your body might still be holding on to it.
Take these few minutes to check in and let go.
[pause 4s]
Sit down and plant your feet on the floor. Close your eyes if you can.
[pause 6s]
Start by noticing. Where do you feel tension right now?
In your chest, your throat, your stomach, your hands?
[pause 15s]
You may notice your mind replaying the scene. A comment, a look, what you wish you'd said.
That's normal. Your brain is trying to make sense of it.
[pause 8s]
When a thought comes back, simply label it. "Replaying." Or "worry." Or "frustration."
You don't need to push it away. Just acknowledge it.
[pause 20s]
Now let's help your body shake off some of that energy.
Gently shake out your hands, as if you were drying them. Let the movement travel up your arms.
[pause 12s]
Roll your shoulders. Shift your feet a little on the floor.
[pause 10s]
And stop. Feel the tingling, the blood moving again.
[pause 8s]
Breathe in deeply through your nose.
And breathe out through your mouth, long and slow, as if you were emptying out the whole meeting.
[pause 8s]
One more time. Breathe in…
And let it go.
[pause 9s]
Keep breathing slowly, with the exhale a little longer than the inhale.
This helps your body calm its stress response.
[pause 25s]
What was said is in the past. What comes next is something you can choose.
[pause 8s]
Ask yourself: how do I want to carry on with my day?
Maybe with more calm. Maybe by taking a step back before you respond.
[pause 18s]
Choose one simple intention. A word, an attitude.
[pause 12s]
Take one last breath, holding that intention close.
[pause 6s]
Then open your eyes, and carry on with your day in your own way.

sessions.title: Screen detox
script: Welcome. Your eyes and your mind have been working hard. Let's give them a real break.
Put your phone down and move away from the screen if you can. Get comfortable.
[pause 6s]
Rub your palms together briskly to warm them up.
[pause 6s]
Then gently cup them over your closed eyes, without pressing.
Let your eyes rest in that warm darkness.
[pause 15s]
Breathe slowly. Feel the warmth of your hands spreading around your eyes.
[pause 20s]
Your eyelids relax. Your brows too. Your forehead widens.
[pause 20s]
Slowly lower your hands, keeping your eyes closed a moment longer.
[pause 6s]
Then open them gently. Let your gaze rest, soft and unfocused, on nothing in particular.
[pause 10s]
Now listen. Let the sounds around you come to you.
The closest ones first. Then the ones farther away.
[pause 20s]
No need to name them. Just let them arrive and fade.
[pause 20s]
Without moving your eyes, widen your attention. Notice what's at the edges of your vision.
To the right. To the left. Above. Below. All at once.
[pause 20s]
This wide, soft gaze is the opposite of a screen. It helps your nervous system slow down.
[pause 15s]
You may feel the urge to check something. A notification, a message.
Let that urge pass, like a wave. It can wait.
[pause 20s]
Breathe. Let your mind slow down to the pace of your breath.
[pause 25s]
There's nothing to scroll here. Just this moment, and you in it.
[pause 15s]
Gently come back to your surroundings. Roll your shoulders, blink a few times.
[pause 6s]
When you return to your screen, try to keep a little of this wide, calm gaze with you.

sessions.title: Close the workday
script: Welcome. Your workday is coming to an end. Let's take the time to close it properly.
Get comfortable. Let your hands rest and your feet feel the floor.
[pause 6s]
Close your eyes. Breathe in deeply through your nose.
And breathe out slowly through your mouth.
[pause 7s]
Once more. Let the exhale carry away a little of the tiredness.
[pause 9s]
Now let your day play back in front of you, like a film. From this morning until now.
There's no need to judge. Just watch what happened.
[pause 30s]
Some moments were easy, others were harder. Both belong here.
[pause 15s]
If an emotion shows up, welcome it. Breathe with it, without holding on.
[pause 25s]
Now pick one thing you did today. Big or small.
An email sent, a problem solved, a moment you truly listened. Something that matters.
[pause 20s]
Acknowledge it. Say to yourself: "I did that."
[pause 15s]
There are probably still things in progress. Unfinished tasks, replies still to send.
Picture a box in front of you. A nice, sturdy box with a lid.
[pause 10s]
One by one, place your unfinished tasks inside. Take your time.
[pause 30s]
They're safe there. They'll wait for you tomorrow, and you'll come back to them rested.
[pause 10s]
Now gently close the lid. Set the box aside.
[pause 15s]
Notice what it feels like not to carry them anymore.
[pause 25s]
It's time to step into your personal time. Let's mark that shift with a small ritual.
Take a big breath in, and as you breathe out, tell yourself: "My workday is done."
[pause 10s]
Rub your hands together, as if washing off the day.
[pause 8s]
Then rest them over your heart. Feel its warmth, its rhythm.
[pause 15s]
Think about what's waiting for you now. Someone you love, a meal, a walk, a quiet moment.
[pause 25s]
Let yourself look forward to it. You've earned it.
[pause 15s]
Take one last slow breath.
[pause 8s]
Gently move your fingers and shoulders. Open your eyes when you're ready.
And step into your evening a little lighter.

sessions.title: Unwind before sleep
script: Good evening. Settle comfortably into your bed, lying on your back or on your side.
[pause 4s]
Let your head sink into the pillow. Your arms rest, heavy and relaxed.
[pause 6s]
Gently close your eyes. The day is over. There is nothing left to do now.
[pause 8s]
Take a slightly deeper breath in through your nose.
[pause 3s]
And breathe out slowly through your mouth, like a long sigh.
[pause 8s]
Once more. Breathe in… and let everything go as you breathe out.
[pause 10s]
Now let's slow the breath down. Breathe in for a count of four. One, two, three, four.
[pause 2s]
Breathe out for a count of six. One, two, three, four, five, six.
[pause 8s]
Keep going at your own pace. Four counts in. Six counts out.
[pause 12s]
A longer exhale helps your body settle. The stress of the day can ease down, little by little.
[pause 19s]
If pictures from the day come back, that's fine. Let them pass without holding on.
[pause 8s]
Imagine each exhale carrying away a small piece of your day. A conversation. A task. A worry.
[pause 24s]
Now bring your attention to your face. Your forehead smooths out. Your brows soften.
[pause 6s]
Your jaw loosens. Your tongue rests easily in your mouth.
[pause 15s]
Your shoulders drop, away from your ears. They have nothing left to carry tonight.
[pause 15s]
Your arms grow heavy. Your hands open, your fingers let go.
[pause 15s]
Your chest rises and falls on its own. Your belly is soft.
[pause 17s]
Your back spreads out across the mattress. Every part of your spine finds its place.
[pause 15s]
Your hips, your thighs, your knees grow heavy.
[pause 12s]
Your calves, your ankles, your feet. Your whole body is resting.
[pause 19s]
Now feel a gentle warmth spreading through you. Like a soft, warm blanket wrapping around you.
[pause 19s]
Your body is heavy. Your body is warm. Your body is safe.
[pause 29s]
There is nothing to get right. Only to let yourself be held.
[pause 29s]
Let your breath find its own rhythm, slow and easy.
[pause 34s]
You can drift… softly…
[pause 34s]
Into sleep.
[pause 39s]
Good night.
[pause 29s]

sessions.title: Heavy body, quiet mind
script: Welcome. Lie down in your bed, in whatever position feels most comfortable.
[pause 5s]
Let your arms rest beside you or on your belly. Close your eyes.
[pause 9s]
Take a big breath in… and let it out slowly.
[pause 9s]
Once more. Breathe in deeply… and breathe out, long and slow.
[pause 12s]
Tonight, you'll let your body become heavy and warm, one part at a time. Nothing to force. You simply notice.
[pause 12s]
Begin with your feet. Feel their weight on the mattress.
[pause 6s]
Say quietly to yourself: my feet are heavy. My feet are heavy and warm.
[pause 21s]
That heaviness rises into your ankles, then into your calves.
[pause 6s]
My legs are heavy. My legs are heavy and warm.
[pause 21s]
Your knees release. Your thighs sink a little deeper into the bed.
[pause 21s]
Your hips grow heavy. Your pelvis rests, fully supported.
[pause 24s]
Now your belly. It rises and falls, gently.
[pause 6s]
A pleasant warmth settles in the center of your belly. Like a small sun.
[pause 24s]
Your back spreads across the mattress. Your lower back, your middle back, your upper back.
[pause 7s]
My back is heavy. My back is heavy and warm.
[pause 24s]
Your chest is calm. Your heart beats quietly, without effort.
[pause 24s]
Your shoulders let go. They slide down toward the mattress.
[pause 6s]
The heaviness flows into your arms. Your elbows, your forearms, your wrists.
[pause 6s]
My arms are heavy. My arms are heavy and warm.
[pause 18s]
Your hands are warm. Your fingers are still and relaxed.
[pause 24s]
Your neck softens. The back of your head rests on the pillow.
[pause 18s]
Your jaw loosens. Your cheeks are soft. Your eyelids are heavy.
[pause 18s]
Your forehead is cool and smooth. Your whole face is peaceful.
[pause 26s]
Now feel your whole body at once. Heavy. Warm. Settled.
[pause 12s]
As if you were slowly sinking into the mattress. Like sinking into warm sand.
[pause 29s]
My body is heavy and warm. My mind is quiet.
[pause 35s]
A body that lets go like this helps stress ease down. There is nothing else to do.
[pause 18s]
To finish, we'll count breaths backward, from twenty down to one. One number for each exhale.
[pause 6s]
If you lose track, that's fine. Pick up wherever you like, or let the numbers fade away.
[pause 6s]
Twenty.
[pause 8s]
Nineteen.
[pause 8s]
Eighteen.
[pause 8s]
Seventeen.
[pause 9s]
Sixteen.
[pause 9s]
Fifteen.
[pause 9s]
Fourteen.
[pause 11s]
Thirteen.
[pause 11s]
Twelve.
[pause 11s]
Eleven.
[pause 12s]
Ten. Keep going on your own, at your own pace.
[pause 40s]
Heavy… warm… quiet…
[pause 40s]
You can let yourself slip into sleep.
[pause 40s]
Good night.
[pause 40s]

sessions.title: Quiet a racing mind
script: Good evening. If your mind is still spinning tonight, you're in the right place.
[pause 3s]
Lie down comfortably. Let your body settle into the bed, and close your eyes.
[pause 9s]
Start with three slow breaths. Breathe in through your nose…
[pause 3s]
and breathe out gently through your mouth.
[pause 9s]
Again. Breathe in… and out.
[pause 9s]
One last time. Breathe in… and let it all go.
[pause 11s]
Tonight, you don't need to silence your thoughts. You're simply going to watch them go by.
[pause 7s]
Notice what shows up in your mind. An idea, a memory, a list of things to do.
[pause 17s]
Notice each thought without judging it. You can simply say to yourself: ah, a thought.
[pause 17s]
Now imagine a wide evening sky, soft and peaceful, above you.
[pause 7s]
Clouds drift slowly across that sky.
[pause 11s]
When a thought arrives, gently place it on a cloud.
[pause 6s]
And watch that cloud float away on the wind, until it disappears over the horizon.
[pause 23s]
Another thought arrives. Place it on a new cloud. Let it go.
[pause 28s]
You don't have to follow the clouds. You stay right here, lying down, watching them pass.
[pause 34s]
Some thoughts are about tomorrow. A meeting, a call, a problem to solve.
[pause 6s]
Imagine a shelf, right beside your bed. The tomorrow shelf.
[pause 6s]
Set each concern on it, one by one. They'll be there in the morning. You'll pick them up when you're rested.
[pause 23s]
Nothing needs solving tonight. Everything can wait.
[pause 23s]
Now come back to your breath. Feel the cool air coming in, the warm air going out.
[pause 9s]
Let your exhale grow a little longer. Slower breathing helps your body calm its stress response.
[pause 28s]
If a thought returns, that's not a failure. Place it on a cloud, and come back to the breath.
[pause 34s]
Now listen to the sounds around you. Near or far.
[pause 7s]
The quiet of the room. Maybe a sound from the street, the hush of the wind.
[pause 23s]
Let sounds come and go, just like the clouds.
[pause 34s]
Your mind is slowing down. Your body is heavy and still.
[pause 40s]
The sky grows calm… the clouds grow few…
[pause 40s]
You can let go now… into sleep.
[pause 40s]
Good night.
[pause 40s]

sessions.title: Back to sleep
script: You've woken up. That's normal, it happens to everyone.
[pause 5s]
Stay lying down. Keep your eyes closed.
[pause 7s]
There's no need to check the time. It doesn't matter right now.
[pause 10s]
You don't have to fall back asleep right away. Lying here, calm and still, is already resting your body.
[pause 15s]
Let your breath slow down. Breathe in gently…
[pause 4s]
and breathe out, a little longer.
[pause 12s]
Again. Breathe in… breathe out, slowly.
[pause 15s]
A long exhale tells your body it's safe to relax.
[pause 24s]
Feel your head, heavy on the pillow.
[pause 18s]
Your shoulders let go.
[pause 18s]
Your arms, your hands, resting.
[pause 22s]
Your belly, soft. Your back, supported.
[pause 22s]
Your legs, heavy.
[pause 18s]
Your feet, at ease.
[pause 30s]
There's nothing to do. Nothing to get right.
[pause 36s]
Just breathing…
[pause 40s]
and resting…
[pause 40s]
Let yourself drift…
[pause 40s]
Sleep well.
[pause 40s]

sessions.title: Gentle wake-up
script: Good morning. Stay in bed a moment longer. There's no rush.
[pause 5s]
Keep your eyes closed if you like. Feel the weight of your body on the mattress.
[pause 11s]
Take a first mindful breath. Breathe in slowly through your nose…
[pause 4s]
and breathe out easily.
[pause 11s]
Once more. Feel the air filling your chest, then your belly.
[pause 13s]
Begin to move your fingers gently. Then your toes.
[pause 11s]
Make small circles with your wrists and your ankles.
[pause 13s]
Now stretch your arms above your head. Lengthen your whole body, from your hands to your feet.
[pause 8s]
Take your time. Stretch like a cat, in whatever direction feels good.
[pause 16s]
Release. Notice how your body is waking up, without any jolt.
[pause 13s]
If you like, turn your head gently to one side, then the other.
[pause 13s]
Imagine the morning light coming into the room. It rests on your face, warm and soft.
[pause 16s]
With every inhale, you welcome a little more of that light. A quiet energy rises in you.
[pause 20s]
Breathe in the brightness of the day… and breathe out what's left of the night.
[pause 16s]
When you feel ready, slowly open your eyes. Let the light in.
[pause 11s]
Take a moment to smile, even a little. This day is starting gently.
[pause 11s]
Have a lovely day.
[pause 7s]

sessions.title: Set your intention
script: Good morning. Sit comfortably, your back upright but relaxed. Rest your hands on your thighs.
[pause 6s]
Close your eyes, or softly lower your gaze.
[pause 9s]
Take a deep breath in… and breathe out slowly.
[pause 12s]
Once more. Feel your feet on the floor, your body grounded.
[pause 15s]
Let your breath return to its natural rhythm. You are here, now, before the day begins.
[pause 23s]
Gently ask yourself: how do I want to move through this day?
[pause 12s]
Let a word come to you. A quality. Maybe calm, patience, confidence, kindness, or joy.
[pause 23s]
There's no right or wrong choice. Simply pick the word that speaks to you this morning.
[pause 18s]
Repeat that word silently as you breathe out. Let it settle inside you.
[pause 27s]
Now imagine your day unfolding. The morning, your first activities, with this word by your side.
[pause 23s]
See yourself at midday. Then in the afternoon. Your word goes with you, like a quiet thread.
[pause 23s]
Now imagine a moment that could feel tense. Something unexpected, a comment, a delay.
[pause 12s]
See yourself pausing. One slow breath. Your shoulders softening.
[pause 15s]
Then you respond with your word. Calmly, in your own way.
[pause 23s]
Breathing slowly in a hard moment helps your body ease its stress response. You can always come back to it.
[pause 18s]
Imagine the end of your day. You feel true to yourself.
[pause 18s]
Take one last deep breath in, welcoming your word.
[pause 5s]
And breathe out, ready to begin.
[pause 12s]
Whenever you like, open your eyes. Your intention comes with you. Have a good day.
[pause 6s]

sessions.title: Natural energy
script: Good morning. Stand up, with your feet hip-width apart.
[pause 4s]
Soften your knees slightly. Let your arms hang by your sides.
[pause 6s]
Feel your feet firmly on the ground. Grow tall, the crown of your head reaching up.
[pause 8s]
Let's wake up the breath. Breathe in actively through your nose, filling your chest.
[pause 3s]
And breathe out through your mouth, simply.
[pause 6s]
A little faster now. Breathe in strongly… out. In… out. In… out.
[pause 8s]
Keep going like this, at your own pace, for a few breaths. Lively, but without straining.
[pause 19s]
Return to a normal breath. Notice the warmth moving through you.
[pause 8s]
Now, with your fingertips, gently tap the top of your chest.
[pause 10s]
Then tap along your arms, from shoulder to hand. One side, then the other.
[pause 15s]
Now shake out your hands, your arms, your shoulders. Let your whole body loosen up.
[pause 15s]
Pause. Feel the tingling, the aliveness in your arms and hands.
[pause 10s]
Breathe in as you raise your arms to the sky…
[pause 4s]
and breathe out as you let them float down.
[pause 6s]
Once more. Breathe in, arms up… breathe out, arms down.
[pause 10s]
You feel awake, present, ready. A calm and steady energy.
[pause 8s]
Off you go. Have a great day.
[pause 4s]

sessions.title: Morning gratitude
script: Good morning. Make yourself comfortable, sitting up or still lying down.
[pause 6s]
Close your eyes and rest one hand on your chest.
[pause 9s]
Take a slow breath in… and breathe out gently.
[pause 12s]
Once more. Feel your hand rise and fall with your breath.
[pause 15s]
This morning, let's take a moment for gratitude. For what's already here.
[pause 9s]
Think of a first thing you're grateful for. It can be very simple. A warm bed, a cup of coffee, the daylight.
[pause 23s]
Notice what you feel as you think of it. Maybe a gentle warmth in your chest.
[pause 19s]
Now a second thing. A moment from yesterday, a small pleasure, something your body lets you do.
[pause 23s]
Let that feeling grow softly beneath your hand.
[pause 19s]
And a third thing. Something you're looking forward to today, even a tiny moment.
[pause 23s]
Breathe with these three things. Breathe in gratitude… breathe out easily.
[pause 19s]
Now think of a person you appreciate. See their face, their smile.
[pause 15s]
Thank them silently. For what they bring you, simply for being who they are.
[pause 23s]
Feel that warmth in your heart. Taking this time helps your body relax and start the day more calmly.
[pause 19s]
Breathe in deeply… and carry this warmth with you.
[pause 12s]
When you're ready, open your eyes. Keep this gratitude with you throughout your day.
[pause 8s]

sessions.title: Full body scan
script: Welcome. Settle into a comfortable position, lying down or seated, with your back well supported.
Let your arms rest by your sides, or your hands on your thighs.
[pause 6s]
If you like, gently close your eyes. Or let your gaze rest on a point in front of you.
[pause 6s]
Take a slightly deeper breath. Breathe in through your nose, and out slowly through your mouth.
[pause 8s]
Once more. Breathe in, and let the air flow out, without effort.
[pause 8s]
Now let your breath find its own rhythm. There is nothing to change.
[pause 8s]
Over the next few minutes, your attention will travel through your body. From your feet all the way to the top of your head.
There is nothing to get right. You are simply noticing what is here, without judgment.
[pause 8s]
Begin with your toes. Notice them, one by one if you can.
Maybe warmth, maybe coolness, a tingling. Or maybe nothing at all. That is perfectly fine.
[pause 15s]
Your attention moves to the soles of your feet, your heels, the tops of your feet.
Feel where they touch the floor, the bed, or the cushion.
[pause 15s]
Slowly move up to your ankles, then your calves.
If you notice any tension, breathe toward it. The in-breath brings it space. The out-breath helps it let go.
[pause 12s]
Now come to your knees. The front, and then the back of the knees.
[pause 10s]
Then your thighs, broad and heavy. Let them sink into the support beneath you.
[pause 12s]
Your attention arrives at your pelvis and your hips. Notice the weight of your body, resting.
[pause 12s]
Now your lower back. This is often a place where we hold tension.
Breathe gently into this area. With each out-breath, let it soften a little.
[pause 12s]
Travel up along your spine, one vertebra at a time, to the space between your shoulder blades.
[pause 15s]
Bring your attention to your belly. Feel it rise as you breathe in, and fall as you breathe out.
[pause 12s]
Then your chest. Your ribcage opening and closing. Perhaps the beating of your heart.
As your breathing slows, your body receives a signal of safety. It can ease its stress response.
[pause 12s]
Come to your shoulders. Notice if they have crept up. Let them drop, just a little.
[pause 15s]
Your attention flows down your arms. Your upper arms, your elbows, your forearms.
[pause 12s]
Your wrists, your palms, each finger right to the fingertips.
[pause 15s]
Now move up to the back of your neck and your throat. Let your head be heavy, fully held.
[pause 15s]
Your face. Your jaw, which can unclench. Your lips, slightly parted.
[pause 12s]
Your cheeks, your nose, your eyes resting behind your eyelids. Your forehead, growing smooth.
[pause 15s]
And finally, the top of your head. Imagine a soft sense of openness there.
[pause 15s]
Now widen your attention to your whole body at once. From your feet to your head, one single whole, breathing.
[pause 15s]
If some area is still calling for your attention, welcome it. Breathe with it, without forcing anything.
[pause 15s]
Stay here, simply present with your whole body.
[pause 20s]
Gently, begin to come back. Let your breath deepen a little.
Wiggle your fingers and toes. Stretch if you feel like it.
[pause 10s]
When you are ready, open your eyes. Carry this calm with you into the rest of your day.

sessions.title: Progressive muscle relaxation
script: Welcome. Find a comfortable position, seated or lying down.
Close your eyes if you wish, and take a long, slow breath.
[pause 10s]
Before we begin, notice your body just as it is right now. Notice the tense areas, and the ones already at ease.
[pause 15s]
In this practice, you will tense one group of muscles for a few seconds, then let it go.
The idea is to feel the difference between tension and relaxation. Tense firmly, but never to the point of pain.
[pause 8s]
Start with your hands. Make fists, tight. Feel the tension in your fingers and palms.
[pause 5s]
And release. Open your hands. Let the relaxation spread.
[pause 20s]
Now your arms. Bend your elbows and tighten your biceps, as if showing off your strength.
[pause 5s]
Release. Let your arms fall, heavy and loose.
[pause 20s]
Notice the contrast. Where there was tension, there is now space.
[pause 8s]
Move to your shoulders. Lift them up toward your ears, as high as you can. Hold.
[pause 5s]
And let them drop all at once. Feel your shoulders sink and widen.
[pause 20s]
Now your face. Squeeze your eyes, scrunch your nose, clench your teeth. Tighten your whole face.
[pause 5s]
Release. Let your forehead smooth out, your jaw fall slightly open.
[pause 20s]
Feel your whole face relax, as if after a long sigh.
[pause 10s]
Take a slow breath. As your muscles let go, your body can calm its stress response.
[pause 10s]
Come to your belly. Tighten your stomach muscles, as if bracing for a small bump. Hold.
[pause 5s]
And release. Let your belly soften, and let your breath settle there.
[pause 20s]
Now your legs. Stretch them out and tighten your thighs, firmly.
[pause 5s]
Release. Feel your legs become heavy and grounded.
[pause 20s]
And finally your feet. Curl your toes downward, and squeeze.
[pause 5s]
And release. Let your feet open, warm and still.
[pause 20s]
Now sweep through your whole body. From your feet up to your face.
If a little tension remains somewhere, let it melt away as you breathe out.
[pause 30s]
Savor this feeling of a relaxed body. Heavy, calm, supported.
[pause 40s]
Gently, deepen your breath. Move your fingers and toes.
[pause 10s]
When you are ready, open your eyes, and come back here, a little lighter.

sessions.title: Shoulders and jaw
script: Welcome. Sit comfortably, your back upright but not stiff.
Rest your hands on your thighs, and take an easy breath.
[pause 6s]
Stress loves to hide in the jaw and the shoulders. For the next few minutes, we will go and find it.
[pause 5s]
Start with your jaw. Are your teeth touching? Let them part a little.
[pause 8s]
Rest your tongue softly against the roof of your mouth, just behind your top teeth. Or simply let it rest.
[pause 8s]
Let your lips soften. Your cheeks relax. The space around your eyes, and your forehead.
[pause 12s]
Now your shoulders. Roll them slowly backward. Once, twice, three times.
[pause 10s]
And the other way, forward. Slowly.
[pause 10s]
Now breathe in as you lift your shoulders up toward your ears.
[pause 4s]
And breathe out as you let them drop. Once more. Lift, and let them fall.
[pause 10s]
Gently tilt your head to the right, ear toward shoulder. Feel the stretch along the left side of your neck.
[pause 12s]
Come back to center. Then tilt to the left.
[pause 12s]
Back to center. Let your chin drop a little toward your chest. Feel the back of your neck lengthen.
[pause 12s]
Slowly lift your head. Breathe gently, letting each out-breath be a little longer than the in-breath.
This slow breathing helps your body release the pressure.
[pause 25s]
Check your jaw again. Loose. Your shoulders. Low and wide.
[pause 25s]
Stay with this ease for a few more breaths.
[pause 25s]
And when you are ready, return to your day, keeping this lightness in your shoulders.

sessions.title: Stress-relief yoga nidra
script: Welcome to this yoga nidra. Lie down on your back, arms by your sides, palms facing up.
Let your legs fall slightly apart. Adjust until you are completely comfortable.
[pause 10s]
Close your eyes. From now on, try to stay still, while remaining awake to the sound of my voice.
[pause 8s]
Take a long breath in, and a long sigh out. Let your body rest with all its weight.
[pause 10s]
Notice the sounds around you, near and far. Let them pass, without holding on.
[pause 15s]
Now choose your intention, your sankalpa. A short, positive phrase, in the present tense.
For example: I am calm and at peace. Or: I take care of myself.
[pause 6s]
Repeat it silently three times, with sincerity.
[pause 28s]
We will now move awareness through the body. Let your attention follow my voice from one part to the next, without effort.
[pause 8s]
Right hand thumb. Index finger. Middle finger. Ring finger. Little finger.
Palm of the hand. Back of the hand. Wrist. Forearm. Elbow. Upper arm. Right shoulder.
Armpit. Right side of the body. Right hip. Thigh. Knee. Calf. Ankle.
Heel. Sole of the foot. Big toe. Second toe. Third. Fourth. Fifth.
[pause 6s]
Left hand thumb. Index finger. Middle finger. Ring finger. Little finger.
Palm of the hand. Back of the hand. Wrist. Forearm. Elbow. Upper arm. Left shoulder.
Armpit. Left side of the body. Left hip. Thigh. Knee. Calf. Ankle.
Heel. Sole of the foot. Big toe. Second toe. Third. Fourth. Fifth.
[pause 6s]
Back of the head. Back of the neck. Right shoulder blade. Left shoulder blade. The whole spine.
Lower back. Buttocks. The whole back, together.
Top of the head. Forehead. Right eyebrow. Left eyebrow. The space between the eyebrows.
Right eye. Left eye. Nose. Right cheek. Left cheek. Lips. Chin. Throat.
Chest. Belly. Navel. Lower belly.
[pause 8s]
The whole right leg. The whole left leg. Both legs together.
The whole right arm. The whole left arm. Both arms together.
The whole back. The whole front of the body. The head. The whole body. The whole body.
[pause 28s]
Now become aware of your natural breath. Air flowing in, air flowing out.
[pause 10s]
You are going to count your breaths backward, from twenty-seven to zero. Breathing in, twenty-seven. Breathing out, twenty-seven. Breathing in, twenty-six. Breathing out, twenty-six.
Continue on your own, at your own pace. If you lose count, simply start again at twenty-seven.
[pause 40s]
[pause 40s]
Now let go of the counting. Return to your natural breath, slow and calm.
This quiet breathing helps your body ease its stress response.
[pause 15s]
Now awaken the feeling of heaviness. Your body is becoming heavy, very heavy.
Your arms are heavy. Your legs are heavy. Your head sinks into the floor.
[pause 28s]
And now, lightness. Your body is becoming light, so light it could float.
Your arms as light as feathers. Your whole body, light as air.
[pause 28s]
Awaken the feeling of warmth. Imagine sunlight on your skin, a gentle warmth wrapping around you.
[pause 24s]
And now, coolness. A cool breeze on your face, the cool water of a stream over your feet.
[pause 24s]
I will name some images. Let each one appear, without effort, then move on to the next.
[pause 4s]
A beach at sunrise.
[pause 8s]
A candle burning in a quiet room.
[pause 8s]
Waves rolling gently onto the sand.
[pause 8s]
A forest after the rain.
[pause 8s]
A starry sky.
[pause 8s]
A still lake, perfectly smooth.
[pause 8s]
A feather slowly falling.
[pause 8s]
A cat asleep in the sun.
[pause 8s]
A mountain covered in snow.
[pause 8s]
A flower slowly opening.
[pause 15s]
Now let your mind rest in the dark, quiet space behind your eyes.
[pause 40s]
Return to your sankalpa, the intention you chose at the beginning. Repeat it three times, with the same sincerity.
It settles deep within you, like a seed in fertile soil.
[pause 28s]
Become aware of your breath. Of your body lying on the floor.
[pause 10s]
Become aware of the sounds around you, of the room you are in.
[pause 10s]
If it is time to return to your day, gently move your fingers and toes. Stretch, roll onto your side, and take your time.
And if it is time to sleep, simply stay where you are, and let yourself drift into rest.
[pause 10s]
This practice of yoga nidra is now complete.

sessions.title: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding
script: Welcome. Stay right where you are, sitting or standing. Keep your eyes open for this practice.
Feel your feet on the ground. Take one slow breath.
[pause 8s]
When anxiety rises, the mind often races into the future. Your senses, though, are always in the present.
We will use them to come back here, to right now.
[pause 5s]
Look around you. Find five things you can see.
Take time to really look at them. Their color, their shape, the way the light falls on them.
[pause 30s]
Good. Now find four things you can touch.
The fabric of your clothes. The surface under your hands. The air on your skin. Feel their texture.
[pause 30s]
Now listen. Find three sounds you can hear.
One sound nearby, one far away. Maybe even the sound of your own breathing.
[pause 30s]
Now two things you can smell.
A scent in the room, on your hands, on your clothes. If you smell nothing, simply notice the air coming in.
[pause 25s]
And finally, one thing you can taste.
The taste in your mouth right now. Or the taste of your last drink.
[pause 20s]
Now come back to your breath. Breathe in slowly through your nose.
[pause 4s]
And breathe out even more slowly. A long out-breath helps your body calm its stress response.
[pause 12s]
Keep going, at your own pace. Breathe in. And breathe out, slowly.
[pause 30s]
Notice how you feel now. A little more present. A little more grounded.
[pause 20s]
You can come back to this practice anytime, anywhere. Five, four, three, two, one.
[pause 5s]
Take one last breath, and ease gently back into your day.

sessions.title: Leaves on a stream
script: Welcome. Make yourself comfortable, and let your eyes gently close.
Take a few slow breaths, and feel your body settle.
[pause 12s]
Imagine you are sitting beside a stream, on a beautiful day.
The water flows gently past you. Listen to its murmur. Feel the grass beneath you.
[pause 12s]
On the water, leaves are drifting by, carried by the current.
[pause 8s]
Now watch your mind. Each time a thought appears, place it on a leaf.
And watch it float away, carried off by the water.
[pause 12s]
It might be a word, an image, a memory, a worry. Whatever it is, it does not matter.
Pleasant thoughts, unpleasant ones, tiny ones. Each one gets its own leaf.
[pause 25s]
You do not need to push the leaves along, or hold them back. The stream does the work.
[pause 30s]
If you notice a thought like: I can't do this, or: this is silly, place that on a leaf too.
[pause 30s]
If a feeling shows up, irritation, sadness, boredom, notice it. And place it on a leaf.
[pause 30s]
At some point, you will probably find yourself swept away by a thought, far from the stream. That is completely normal.
As soon as you notice, simply come back to the water's edge, and place that thought on a leaf.
[pause 35s]
Your thoughts are just thoughts. They come, and they go. You are the one watching them pass.
[pause 35s]
Keep going, at your own pace. One thought, one leaf. And the stream, flowing on.
[pause 40s]
If no thoughts come for a while, simply watch the water flow.
[pause 35s]
Now let the image of the stream gently fade.
[pause 6s]
Come back to your breath. Feel the weight of your body, the support beneath you.
[pause 12s]
Move your hands and feet a little.
[pause 5s]
And when you are ready, open your eyes. Remember, you can always let a thought float away on a leaf.

sessions.title: Meet your emotion (RAIN)
script: Welcome. Settle in comfortably, and close your eyes if you wish.
Take a few slow breaths, and let your body settle.
[pause 10s]
We will practice RAIN, a gentle way to meet a difficult emotion.
Recognize. Allow. Investigate with kindness. Nurture.
[pause 6s]
Think of a situation that is on your mind right now. Not the heaviest one, something manageable.
[pause 12s]
The first step is to recognize. What are you feeling, right here, right now?
Try to simply name the emotion. Worry. Anger. Sadness. Fear.
[pause 25s]
The second step is to allow. Let this emotion be here, just as it is.
You don't have to like it, or push it away. You can tell yourself: this is here, and that's okay.
[pause 30s]
The third step is to investigate, with kindness. Where do you feel this emotion in your body?
Maybe a tight throat, a heavy chest, a knot in your stomach.
[pause 25s]
Approach this sensation with curiosity, the way you might approach a small, frightened animal.
Is it warm or cool? Solid or shifting? Breathe gently around it.
[pause 30s]
Ask it, softly: what do you need?
[pause 25s]
The fourth step is to nurture. Place a hand on your heart, or wherever the emotion lives.
Feel the warmth of your hand. This simple gesture can help your body feel safe.
[pause 15s]
Offer yourself a few kind words, as you would to a dear friend. Maybe: I'm here. Or: this is hard, and I'm taking care of myself.
[pause 30s]
Let these words settle into you. Breathe slowly.
[pause 30s]
Notice how you feel now. Nothing needs to have gone away. You have simply made room for what is here.
[pause 25s]
Keep your hand on your heart for a moment longer.
[pause 10s]
Then gently come back. Feel your body, and the room around you.
[pause 6s]
And when you are ready, open your eyes, carrying a little more kindness toward yourself.

sessions.title: Set your worries down
script: Welcome. This is a time to set down some of what you are carrying.
Find a comfortable position, seated or lying down. Let your shoulders drop and your hands rest.
[pause 6s]
Close your eyes if that feels right, or soften your gaze toward the floor.
[pause 5s]
Take a slow breath in through your nose. And let it go through your mouth, a little longer than the inhale.
[pause 8s]
Once more. Breathe in slowly. And breathe out, letting the body settle.
[pause 10s]
Slow breathing like this helps your body ease its stress response. There is nothing to fix right now.
[pause 8s]
Now, gently, let your worries come to mind. Not to solve them. Just to see them.
[pause 8s]
Name the first one quietly to yourself. A word or a short phrase is enough.
[pause 12s]
Notice where you feel it in the body. Maybe the chest, the stomach, the jaw.
[pause 10s]
Now let a second worry appear. Name it too.
[pause 12s]
And if there is a third, give it a name as well.
[pause 12s]
You don't need to name everything. Three or four is plenty for today.
[pause 8s]
Now we are going to sort them. Take each worry and ask one simple question.
Is there something I can do about this? Or is it outside my control?
[pause 10s]
Go through them one by one. Place each on one side or the other.
[pause 20s]
Some worries may sit in between. That's fine. Just notice which part you can act on.
[pause 10s]
Now return to the first worry on the side of things you can act on.
What is one small next step? Something simple, something you could do today or tomorrow.
[pause 12s]
Keep it small. Sending a message. Writing a note. Asking for help.
[pause 10s]
Picture yourself taking that step. See how it feels to move, even a little.
[pause 12s]
Now turn to the worries outside your control.
Imagine a quiet bench in a garden, or a wooden box with a lid. Choose whichever feels right.
[pause 10s]
One at a time, set each of these worries down there.
[pause 16s]
You are not throwing them away. You are simply letting them rest, for now, outside of you.
[pause 12s]
If one tries to come back, that's okay. Gently set it down again.
[pause 12s]
Now bring your attention back to your breath.
Feel the air coming in. Feel it going out.
[pause 12s]
With each exhale, let your body grow a little lighter.
[pause 24s]
Simply rest here, breathing, with nothing to carry.
[pause 28s]
Notice the space that is here now. A little more room inside.
[pause 16s]
Slowly, begin to come back. Move your fingers and your toes.
[pause 8s]
Remember your one small step. And know that your worries will wait on the bench.
[pause 6s]
When you are ready, open your eyes. Take this calm with you.

sessions.title: Self-compassion break
script: Welcome. Let's take a short, kind pause together.
Sit comfortably and let your body be supported. Close your eyes if you like.
[pause 6s]
Take a slow breath in. And a long breath out.
[pause 8s]
Bring to mind something that feels difficult right now. Something small to medium, not the hardest thing.
[pause 12s]
Let yourself feel it a little. Notice where it shows up in your body.
[pause 12s]
Now say to yourself, softly: this is a moment of difficulty.
[pause 6s]
This hurts. This is hard.
[pause 17s]
Now remind yourself: difficulty is part of life. I am not alone in this.
[pause 6s]
Right now, many people feel something similar. You are part of a very human experience.
[pause 17s]
Now place one hand on your heart, or wherever feels soothing.
[pause 6s]
Feel the warmth of your hand. Feel the gentle rise and fall of your breath beneath it.
[pause 12s]
And say to yourself: may I be kind to myself.
[pause 8s]
May I give myself the care I need.
[pause 22s]
If other words come, words a good friend might say, let them come too.
[pause 28s]
Rest here for a few breaths, held by your own kindness.
[pause 33s]
Gently let your hand come down. Take one more slow breath.
[pause 6s]
When you're ready, open your eyes. You can return to this pause anytime.

sessions.title: Loving-kindness
script: Welcome. In this practice, we will offer kind wishes, first to ourselves, then outward.
Settle into a comfortable position. Let your spine be tall and your face soft.
[pause 6s]
Take a few slow breaths. Let each exhale be a little longer than the inhale.
[pause 12s]
Let your breath find its own easy rhythm.
[pause 8s]
Begin with yourself. Picture yourself as you are right now, sitting here.
[pause 8s]
Silently offer yourself these words. May I be safe.
[pause 6s]
May I be healthy.
[pause 6s]
May I be at peace.
[pause 6s]
May I live with ease.
[pause 19s]
If the words feel strange, that's okay. Simply offer the intention.
[pause 8s]
Once more, slowly. May I be safe. May I be healthy. May I be at peace. May I live with ease.
[pause 25s]
Now bring to mind someone you love easily. A friend, a family member, even a pet.
[pause 8s]
See their face. Feel the warmth that comes when you think of them.
[pause 8s]
May you be safe.
[pause 6s]
May you be healthy.
[pause 6s]
May you be at peace.
[pause 6s]
May you live with ease.
[pause 25s]
Now think of someone neutral. Someone you see but don't really know. A neighbor, a cashier, a passerby.
[pause 8s]
They too want to be happy. They too have their worries.
[pause 6s]
May you be safe. May you be healthy.
[pause 6s]
May you be at peace. May you live with ease.
[pause 25s]
Now, gently, bring to mind someone you find a little difficult. Not the hardest person. Someone who irritates you slightly.
[pause 10s]
Notice any resistance. You can keep a little distance. Go only as far as feels okay.
[pause 8s]
May you be safe.
[pause 6s]
May you be healthy.
[pause 6s]
May you be at peace.
[pause 6s]
May you live with ease.
[pause 19s]
If this feels too hard, return to wishing yourself well. That is part of the practice too.
[pause 19s]
Now let your kindness widen. To everyone in this building, this street, this city.
[pause 10s]
To people near and far. To all living beings, everywhere.
[pause 8s]
May all beings be safe.
[pause 6s]
May all beings be healthy.
[pause 6s]
May all beings be at peace.
[pause 6s]
May all beings live with ease.
[pause 37s]
Rest in this feeling of warmth. Let it fill you, and spread out from you.
[pause 40s]
Slowly bring your attention back to your breath, and to your body.
[pause 8s]
Wiggle your fingers. Take a deeper breath.
[pause 6s]
When you are ready, open your eyes. Carry this kindness into your day.

sessions.title: Soften your inner critic
script: Welcome. Today we will meet your inner critic, with curiosity and with kindness.
Get comfortable. Let your hands rest and your jaw soften.
[pause 6s]
Take a slow breath in. And a slow breath out.
[pause 8s]
Again. In. And out, letting go a little more.
[pause 10s]
Now recall a recent moment when you were hard on yourself. A mistake, a missed goal, a moment you felt not good enough.
[pause 12s]
Listen for the voice that spoke. What did it say? Hear the exact words if you can.
[pause 16s]
Notice its tone. Is it sharp? Cold? Impatient?
[pause 10s]
Notice how your body responds. Maybe a tightness, a sinking, a heat.
[pause 12s]
You are not this voice. You are the one who hears it.
[pause 10s]
Now consider this. This voice, as harsh as it sounds, is often trying to protect you.
It may want to keep you safe from failure, from rejection, from being hurt.
[pause 16s]
What might it be afraid of? Let the answer come on its own.
[pause 19s]
See if you can thank it, even a little. Thank you for trying to protect me.
[pause 8s]
I understand. And I can take it from here.
[pause 16s]
Now imagine a kind friend sitting beside you. Someone who truly cares for you.
[pause 8s]
If they heard what you went through, what would they say? How would they say it?
[pause 19s]
Notice their warmth. Their patience. The way they see the whole of you.
[pause 12s]
Now go back to the critic's sentence. Let's rewrite it together.
Keep the truth in it, but change the tone. Speak as that kind friend would.
[pause 12s]
For example, instead of: you always mess up. Perhaps: that was hard, and you are learning.
[pause 10s]
Find your own new sentence. Say it silently to yourself.
[pause 21s]
Say it again, slowly. Let the words land in your body.
[pause 21s]
Notice any shift. Even a small softening counts.
[pause 16s]
Place a hand on your chest if you like, and breathe with this kinder voice.
[pause 31s]
You can return to this new sentence whenever the critic speaks up.
[pause 10s]
Take one more slow breath. Move your fingers and shoulders gently.
[pause 6s]
When you're ready, open your eyes. Be your own good friend today.

sessions.title: Single-point focus
script: Welcome. This practice trains your attention, one breath at a time.
Sit upright and relaxed. Rest your hands on your thighs and close your eyes.
[pause 6s]
Take a couple of slower breaths to settle in.
[pause 10s]
Now let your breath return to its natural pace.
[pause 5s]
Bring your attention to the tip of your nose, at the nostrils.
Notice the air as it comes in. Maybe a little cooler. And as it leaves, a little warmer.
[pause 12s]
Keep your attention right there, on that one small point.
[pause 10s]
Now we'll add counting. On the next out-breath, count one. On the next, two.
Count up to ten, then begin again at one.
[pause 8s]
If you lose count, or go past ten, simply start again at one. No judgment.
[pause 26s]
Keep counting, breath by breath, attention resting at the nostrils.
[pause 30s]
At some point, your mind will wander. That is completely normal.
When you notice it, gently let the thought go and return to the breath. Start again at one.
[pause 26s]
That moment of noticing and returning is the training. Each return makes your focus stronger.
[pause 30s]
Stay with it. In at the nostrils. Out at the nostrils. One count at a time.
[pause 30s]
If you feel restless, simply notice it, and return.
[pause 26s]
Now let go of the counting. Just rest your attention on the breath for a few moments.
[pause 17s]
Take a deeper breath in. And let it go.
[pause 5s]
When you're ready, open your eyes. Bring this clear focus with you.

sessions.title: Before an important task
script: Welcome. Let's take a few minutes to prepare, calmly and clearly.
Sit upright, feet flat on the floor. Let your shoulders relax.
[pause 5s]
If you feel nervous, that's okay. It means this matters to you.
[pause 5s]
We'll do a few rounds of box breathing. Four counts in, four hold, four out, four hold.
Breathe in, two, three, four.
[pause 4s]
Hold, two, three, four.
[pause 4s]
Breathe out, two, three, four.
[pause 4s]
Hold, two, three, four.
[pause 4s]
Again. In, two, three, four.
[pause 4s]
Hold.
[pause 4s]
Out, two, three, four.
[pause 4s]
Hold.
[pause 4s]
Continue on your own for a few more rounds.
[pause 40s]
Good. Let your breath return to normal. Notice your body feeling steadier.
[pause 8s]
Now think of the task ahead. Not the whole thing. Just the very first concrete step.
[pause 10s]
See it clearly. Opening the document. Writing the first line. Making the first call.
[pause 12s]
Picture yourself doing that step, calm and focused.
[pause 12s]
Now set a clear intention. Say it silently. For example: I will give this my full attention for the next while.
[pause 12s]
Take one more full breath in. And out.
[pause 5s]
Open your eyes. Start now, with that first step.

sessions.title: Mindful breathing
script: Welcome. This is a practice of simply being with your breath.
Find a posture that is both relaxed and alert. Let your back be straight but not stiff.
[pause 6s]
Rest your hands wherever they are comfortable. Gently close your eyes.
[pause 8s]
Take a moment to arrive. Notice the weight of your body, and the points where it is supported.
[pause 12s]
Take two or three deeper breaths, letting each exhale release a little tension.
[pause 12s]
Now let your breath be natural. There is no need to control it.
[pause 10s]
Bring your attention to your belly. Feel it gently rise as you breathe in, and fall as you breathe out.
[pause 12s]
Just feeling. No need to change anything.
[pause 16s]
Now let your attention move up to your chest. Notice how it expands and settles with each breath.
[pause 16s]
Perhaps you feel the ribs widening, the movement in your back.
[pause 16s]
Now bring your attention to your nostrils. Notice the air coming in, and going out.
[pause 12s]
The slight coolness of the in-breath. The warmth of the out-breath.
[pause 16s]
Choose the place where the breath feels clearest for you. Let your attention rest there.
[pause 25s]
Your mind will wander. Thoughts, plans, memories will appear. This is what minds do.
When you notice you're thinking, gently note it: thinking. Then return to the breath.
[pause 25s]
No need to push thoughts away. Just note, and return. Again and again.
[pause 33s]
Each time you return, you are training a calm and steady attention.
[pause 33s]
Breathing in, knowing you are breathing in. Breathing out, knowing you are breathing out.
[pause 33s]
If sounds or sensations pull at you, note them too. Hearing. Feeling. Then come back.
[pause 33s]
Now let your attention widen. From the breath, to the whole body breathing.
[pause 12s]
Feel your body as one whole. Sitting. Breathing. Alive.
[pause 25s]
Notice sensations anywhere. Warmth, coolness, tingling, pressure. Let them all be here.
[pause 29s]
Now widen even further. Let go of any single focus.
Simply be aware. Of sounds, sensations, thoughts, the breath. Whatever arises.
[pause 16s]
Like the sky letting clouds pass through, let everything come and go.
[pause 33s]
Rest in this open awareness.
[pause 33s]
As you breathe this slowly, your body can ease out of its stress response. Let it.
[pause 25s]
Now gently bring your attention back to the breath, one last time.
[pause 12s]
Begin to deepen your breathing. Feel the room around you.
[pause 8s]
Move your fingers and toes. Stretch if you'd like.
[pause 8s]
When you are ready, open your eyes. Take this steady presence into the rest of your day.
